TEXT.source: kanakanavu.info, "Mo'o 2014 Story 1", https://kanakanavu.info/language-documentation/moo-2014-story-1.html. This story was recorded by Ilka Wild in collaboration with Elizabeth Zeitoun in March 2014 in Namasia village. The speaker is Mo'o Kangena.

S.FORM: una kan kanakanavu miena makai kari maku mison.
S.PHON: una kan kanakanavu miena makai ka[r|ɾ]i maku mison
S.FORM: una kan kanakanavu miena makai kari maku mison.
S.PHON: una kan kanakanavu miena makai ka[r|ɾ]i maku mison
S.TRANSL: There used to be a Kanakanavu long ago on which I have a story to tell.

S.FORM: sua iisua ia kinaraʉva kan maakari kan sua sarone-in kan ia tia s<um>asʉrʉcʉ ringei.
S.PHON: sua iisua ia kina[r|ɾ]aɨva kan maaka[r|ɾ]i kan sua sa[r|ɾ]onein kan ia tia sumasɨ[r|ɾ]ɨʦɨ [r|ɾ]iŋei
S.FORM: sua iisua ia kinaraʉva kan maakari kan sua saronein kan ia tia sumasʉrʉcʉ ringei.
S.PHON: sua iisua ia kina[r|ɾ]aɨva kan maaka[r|ɾ]i kan sua sa[r|ɾ]onein kan ia tia sumasɨ[r|ɾ]ɨʦɨ [r|ɾ]iŋei
S.TRANSL: As for that, a couple discussed that the husband was going to see a trap.

S.FORM: sua 'ucang-in ia tia mukusa kan umoo'uma.
S.PHON: sua ʔuʦaŋin ia tia mukusa kan umooʔuma
S.FORM: sua 'ucangin ia tia mukusa kan umoo'uma.
S.PHON: sua ʔuʦaŋin ia tia mukusa kan umooʔuma
S.TRANSL: As for his spouse, she went towards the field.

S.FORM: makasua sua timana maku sua po'ʉ'ʉna miena cucuru kara'e.
S.PHON: makasua sua timana maku sua poʔɨʔɨna miena ʦuʦu[r|ɾ]u ka[r|ɾ]aʔe
S.FORM: makasua sua timana maku sua po'ʉ'ʉna miena cucuru kara'e.
S.PHON: makasua sua timana maku sua poʔɨʔɨna miena ʦuʦu[r|ɾ]u ka[r|ɾ]aʔe
S.TRANSL: I heard that telling long ago (but don't know) if it is real or not.

S.FORM: makaasi kan saronei:
S.PHON: makaasi kan sa[r|ɾ]onei
S.FORM: makaasi kan saronei:
S.PHON: makaasi kan sa[r|ɾ]onei
S.TRANSL: The man said:

S.FORM: tee ku mukusa rumura s<um>asʉrʉcʉ ringei misa kan.
S.PHON: tee ku mukusa [r|ɾ]umu[r|ɾ]a sumasɨ[r|ɾ]ɨʦɨ [r|ɾ]iŋei misa kan
S.FORM: tee ku mukusa rumura sumasʉrʉcʉ ringei misa kan.
S.PHON: tee ku mukusa [r|ɾ]umu[r|ɾ]a sumasɨ[r|ɾ]ɨʦɨ [r|ɾ]iŋei misa kan
S.TRANSL: "I will go in the jungle to control the traps." he said.

S.FORM: ucang-in ia tee kan mukusa umoo'uma.
S.PHON: uʦaŋin ia tee kan mukusa umooʔuma
S.FORM: ucangin ia tee kan mukusa umoo'uma.
S.PHON: uʦaŋin ia tee kan mukusa umooʔuma
S.TRANSL: As for his wife, she went to the field.

S.FORM: nakai sua ucang-in ia makaasi makaasi kan tuturuani na tanʉvin matu'apuru kan cu ucang-in.
S.PHON: nakai sua uʦaŋin ia makaasi makaasi kan tutu[r|ɾ]uani na tanɨvin matuʔapu[r|ɾ]u kan ʦu uʦaŋin
S.FORM: nakai sua ucangin ia makaasi makaasi kan tuturuani na tanʉvin matu'apuru kan cu ucangin.
S.PHON: nakai sua uʦaŋin ia makaasi makaasi kan tutu[r|ɾ]uani na tanɨvin matuʔapu[r|ɾ]u kan ʦu uʦaŋin
S.TRANSL: But for his wife, she went, went towards a hut (for workers) and made fire.

S.FORM: tee kan ʉsʉ-ʉn kei 'inia manu-in na apuru si una kan sikuurapʉ.
S.PHON: tee kan ɨsɨɨn kei ʔinia manuin na apu[r|ɾ]u si una kan sikuu[r|ɾ]apɨ
S.FORM: tee kan ʉsʉʉn kei 'inia manuin na apuru si una kan sikuurapʉ.
S.PHON: tee kan ɨsɨɨn kei ʔinia manuin na apu[r|ɾ]u si una kan sikuu[r|ɾ]apɨ
S.TRANSL: She put her child be next to fire because there are mosquitos.

S.FORM: makasua sua ucang-in um-ʉkuru kan tooku mukusa kukuca kan taro'an.
S.PHON: makasua sua uʦaŋin umɨku[r|ɾ]u kan tooku mukusa kukuʦa kan ta[r|ɾ]oʔan
S.FORM: makasua sua ucangin umʉkuru kan tooku mukusa kukuca kan taro'an.
S.PHON: makasua sua uʦaŋin umɨku[r|ɾ]u kan tooku mukusa kukuʦa kan ta[r|ɾ]oʔan
S.TRANSL: And then his wife took a hoe and went behind the hut.

S.FORM: tee kan makituku kan cʉn si sua manu isua ia ka'an kan t<um>atang.
S.PHON: tee kan makituku kan ʦɨn si sua manu isua ia kaʔan kan tumataŋ
S.FORM: tee kan makituku kan cʉn si sua manu isua ia ka'an kan tumatang.
S.PHON: tee kan makituku kan ʦɨn si sua manu isua ia kaʔan kan tumataŋ
S.TRANSL: She took the hoe for the grass because that child did not cry.

S.FORM: mu-'una kan inia cine-in mo'oma matavʉcʉkei taniarʉ.
S.PHON: muʔuna kan inia ʦinein moʔoma matavɨʦɨkei tania[r|ɾ]ɨ
S.FORM: mu'una kan inia cinein mo'oma matavʉcʉkei taniarʉ.
S.PHON: muʔuna kan inia ʦinein moʔoma matavɨʦɨkei tania[r|ɾ]ɨ
S.TRANSL: It's mother was there working (until) noontime.

S.FORM: makaasi kan cine-in atimiseen ka'an t<um>atang manu maku misa kan.
S.PHON: makaasi kan ʦinein atimiseen kaʔan tumataŋ manu maku misa kan
S.FORM: makaasi kan cinein atimiseen ka'an tumatang manu maku misa kan.
S.PHON: makaasi kan ʦinein atimiseen kaʔan tumataŋ manu maku misa kan
S.TRANSL: "Why doesn't my child cry?", his mother said.

S.FORM: si sua cine-in ia k<um>akoru kan cʉn ni-mʉtʉa kan vʉnei ngcou vʉnei arakʉpʉ mastatiana sua vʉnei.
S.PHON: si sua ʦinein ia kumako[r|ɾ]u kan ʦɨn nimɨtɨa kan vɨnei ŋʦou vɨnei a[r|ɾ]akɨpɨ mastatiana sua vɨnei
S.FORM: si sua cinein ia kumakoru kan cʉn nimʉtʉa kan vʉnei ngcou vʉnei arakʉpʉ mastatiana sua vʉnei.
S.PHON: si sua ʦinein ia kumako[r|ɾ]u kan ʦɨn nimɨtɨa kan vɨnei ŋʦou vɨnei a[r|ɾ]akɨpɨ mastatiana sua vɨnei
S.TRANSL: Since it's mother diged in the grass, she found a snake curling, there was such a big snake.

S.FORM: ni-vua kan kei manu-in tia apati-muamuarʉ.
S.PHON: nivua kan kei manuin tia apatimuamua[r|ɾ]ɨ
S.FORM: nivua kan kei manuin tia apatimuamuarʉ.
S.PHON: nivua kan kei manuin tia apatimuamua[r|ɾ]ɨ
S.TRANSL: She gave it to her child and let it play.

S.FORM: si sua cʉpʉng cine-in ia ka'an tia r<um>ara'isi vʉnei iisi misei.
S.PHON: si sua ʦɨpɨŋ ʦinein ia kaʔan tia [r|ɾ]uma[r|ɾ]aʔisi vɨnei iisi misei
S.FORM: si sua cʉpʉng cinein ia ka'an tia rumara'isi vʉnei iisi misei.
S.PHON: si sua ʦɨpɨŋ ʦinein ia kaʔan tia [r|ɾ]uma[r|ɾ]aʔisi vɨnei iisi misei
S.TRANSL: Because in it's mother's mind this snake won't bite.

S.FORM: sua vʉnei ia ni-vua kei manu-in apati-muamuarʉ ʉkʉr-ei sua manu-in.
S.PHON: sua vɨnei ia nivua kei manuin apatimuamua[r|ɾ]ɨ ɨkɨ[r|ɾ]ei sua manuin
S.FORM: sua vʉnei ia nivua kei manuin apatimuamuarʉ ʉkʉrei sua manuin.
S.PHON: sua vɨnei ia nivua kei manuin apatimuamua[r|ɾ]ɨ ɨkɨ[r|ɾ]ei sua manuin
S.TRANSL: As for the snake, she gave it to the child to grab and let it play (with it).

S.FORM: mati-muamuarʉ manasi ni-ra'isi vʉnei manana ramucu-in ni-ra'isi kei.
S.PHON: matimuamua[r|ɾ]ɨ manasi ni[r|ɾ]aʔisi vɨnei manana [r|ɾ]amuʦuin ni[r|ɾ]aʔisi kei
S.FORM: matimuamuarʉ manasi nira'isi vʉnei manana ramucuin nira'isi kei.
S.PHON: matimuamua[r|ɾ]ɨ manasi ni[r|ɾ]aʔisi vɨnei manana [r|ɾ]amuʦuin ni[r|ɾ]aʔisi kei
S.TRANSL: ...(the child) played so that the snake bit it's right hand.

S.FORM: makaasi kan cine-in miseen manu mita ka'aan t<um>atang mata-vʉcʉkei sua taniarʉ misa kan.
S.PHON: makaasi kan ʦinein miseen manu mita kaʔaan tumataŋ matavɨʦɨkei sua tania[r|ɾ]ɨ misa kan
S.FORM: makaasi kan cinein miseen manu mita ka'aan tumatang matavʉcʉkei sua taniarʉ misa kan.
S.PHON: makaasi kan ʦinein miseen manu mita kaʔaan tumataŋ matavɨʦɨkei sua tania[r|ɾ]ɨ misa kan
S.TRANSL: And then the it's mother said: "Why is our child not crying, it's is already noon time." she said.

S.FORM: mukusa kan inia cine-in mecau na taro'an akia manu-in s<in>cʉpʉ kan sua manu-in.
S.PHON: mukusa kan inia ʦinein meʦau na ta[r|ɾ]oʔan akia manuin sinʦɨpɨ kan sua manuin
S.FORM: mukusa kan inia cinein mecau na taro'an akia manuin sincʉpʉ kan sua manuin.
S.PHON: mukusa kan inia ʦinein meʦau na ta[r|ɾ]oʔan akia manuin sinʦɨpɨ kan sua manuin
S.TRANSL: The mother peeked at the kid, but nothing, the kid was sleeping.

S.FORM: mukusa kan inia manu meimei meimei misa kan ka'aan kan aramia'ʉ.
S.PHON: mukusa kan inia manu meimei meimei misa kan kaʔaan kan a[r|ɾ]amiaʔɨ
S.FORM: mukusa kan inia manu meimei meimei misa kan ka'aan kan aramia'ʉ.
S.PHON: mukusa kan inia manu meimei meimei misa kan kaʔaan kan a[r|ɾ]amiaʔɨ
S.TRANSL: The mother went there: "Child!" she said, but the child won't awake.

S.FORM: pati'ʉnʉ'ʉn-ei kan inia masikoocun.
S.PHON: patiʔɨnɨʔɨnei kan inia masikooʦun
S.FORM: pati'ʉnʉ'ʉnei kan inia masikoocun.
S.PHON: patiʔɨnɨʔɨnei kan inia masikooʦun
S.TRANSL: The mother pinched her again.

S.FORM: meimei meimei misa kan.
S.PHON: meimei meimei misa kan
S.FORM: meimei meimei misa kan.
S.PHON: meimei meimei misa kan
S.TRANSL: "Little sister!" she said.

S.FORM: ka'aan cu murungisa.
S.PHON: kaʔaan ʦu mu[r|ɾ]uŋisa
S.FORM: ka'aan cu murungisa.
S.PHON: kaʔaan ʦu mu[r|ɾ]uŋisa
S.TRANSL: She didn't breathe.

S.FORM: ʉkʉr-ei kan inia vʉcʉke-in akia cu.
S.PHON: ɨkɨ[r|ɾ]ei kan inia vɨʦɨkein akia ʦu
S.FORM: ʉkʉrei kan inia vʉcʉkein akia cu.
S.PHON: ɨkɨ[r|ɾ]ei kan inia vɨʦɨkein akia ʦu
S.TRANSL: She touched her belly, but nothing.

S.FORM: tavara'ʉ cu kan cine-in.
S.PHON: tava[r|ɾ]aʔɨ ʦu kan ʦinein
S.FORM: tavara'ʉ cu kan cinein.
S.PHON: tava[r|ɾ]aʔɨ ʦu kan ʦinein
S.TRANSL: The mother knew.

S.FORM: ah, acu kan ni-ra'isi vʉnei iisi misa kan.
S.PHON: ah aʦu kan ni[r|ɾ]aʔisi vɨnei iisi misa kan
S.FORM: ah, acu kan nira'isi vʉnei iisi misa kan.
S.PHON: ah aʦu kan ni[r|ɾ]aʔisi vɨnei iisi misa kan
S.TRANSL: "Ah, the kid must have been biten by a snake." she said.

S.FORM: ni-macei sua manu.
S.PHON: nimaʦei sua manu
S.FORM: nimacei sua manu.
S.PHON: nimaʦei sua manu
S.TRANSL: The child was dead.

S.FORM: mu-'una cu kan inia cine-in tia puukarikari ngcou 'esi cu t<um>atang 'esi kan t<um>atang makaasi kan manu manu misei.
S.PHON: muʔuna ʦu kan inia ʦinein tia puuka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]i ŋʦou ʔesi ʦu tumataŋ ʔesi kan tumataŋ makaasi kan manu manu misei
S.FORM: mu'una cu kan inia cinein tia puukarikari ngcou 'esi cu tumatang 'esi kan tumatang makaasi kan manu manu misei.
S.PHON: muʔuna ʦu kan inia ʦinein tia puuka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]i ŋʦou ʔesi ʦu tumataŋ ʔesi kan tumataŋ makaasi kan manu manu misei
S.TRANSL: His mom was there speaking, was crying and crying: Child, child!" she said.

S.FORM: ka'aan cu marivari manu.
S.PHON: kaʔaan ʦu ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]i manu
S.FORM: ka'aan cu marivari manu.
S.PHON: kaʔaan ʦu ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]i manu
S.TRANSL: The child didn't answer.

S.FORM: avei inia.
S.PHON: avei inia
S.FORM: avei inia.
S.PHON: avei inia
S.TRANSL: She took her.

S.FORM: mukusa tanasa.
S.PHON: mukusa tanasa
S.FORM: mukusa tanasa.
S.PHON: mukusa tanasa
S.TRANSL: (She) went home.

S.FORM: makasi kan saronei esi cu kan tanasa ni-puringei kan takuisi.
S.PHON: makasi kan sa[r|ɾ]onei esi ʦu kan tanasa nipu[r|ɾ]iŋei kan takuisi
S.FORM: makasi kan saronei esi cu kan tanasa nipuringei kan takuisi.
S.PHON: makasi kan sa[r|ɾ]onei esi ʦu kan tanasa nipu[r|ɾ]iŋei kan takuisi
S.TRANSL: The husband was already home with the caught goat.

S.FORM: pukari-in kan saronei neen vanei su t<um>atang misa kan.
S.PHON: puka[r|ɾ]iin kan sa[r|ɾ]onei neen vanei su tumataŋ misa kan
S.FORM: pukariin kan saronei neen vanei su tumatang misa kan.
S.PHON: puka[r|ɾ]iin kan sa[r|ɾ]onei neen vanei su tumataŋ misa kan
S.TRANSL: He said to his wife: "Why do you cry?" he said.

S.FORM: ni-'ava kan kei manu-in neen vanei su t<um>atang?
S.PHON: niʔava kan kei manuin neen vanei su tumataŋ
S.FORM: ni'ava kan kei manuin neen vanei su tumatang?
S.PHON: niʔava kan kei manuin neen vanei su tumataŋ
S.TRANSL: "You carried your child, why do you cry?"

S.FORM: ka'an kan marivari.
S.PHON: kaʔan kan ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]i
S.FORM: ka'an kan marivari.
S.PHON: kaʔan kan ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]i
S.TRANSL: His wife didn't answer.

S.FORM: pasi-ʉnʉ'ʉn-ei kan inia ka'an kan marimari.
S.PHON: pasiɨnɨʔɨnei kan inia kaʔan kan ma[r|ɾ]ima[r|ɾ]i
S.FORM: pasiʉnʉ'ʉnei kan inia ka'an kan marimari.
S.PHON: pasiɨnɨʔɨnei kan inia kaʔan kan ma[r|ɾ]ima[r|ɾ]i
S.TRANSL: He asked her again and she still didn't answer.

S.FORM: ucangʉ o misa kan.
S.PHON: uʦaŋɨ o misa kan
S.FORM: ucangʉ o misa kan.
S.PHON: uʦaŋɨ o misa kan
S.TRANSL: "Wife!" he said.

S.FORM: ka'aan marivari.
S.PHON: kaʔaan ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]i
S.FORM: ka'aan marivari.
S.PHON: kaʔaan ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]i
S.TRANSL: (She) still didn't answer.

S.FORM: cʉ'ʉr-ei kan inia manu akia cu ni-macei neen vanei-in?
S.PHON: ʦɨʔɨ[r|ɾ]ei kan inia manu akia ʦu nimaʦei neen vaneiin
S.FORM: cʉ'ʉrei kan inia manu akia cu nimacei neen vaneiin?
S.PHON: ʦɨʔɨ[r|ɾ]ei kan inia manu akia ʦu nimaʦei neen vaneiin
S.TRANSL: The husband saw the kid was dead, how come?

S.FORM: makari kan saronei:
S.PHON: maka[r|ɾ]i kan sa[r|ɾ]onei
S.FORM: makari kan saronei:
S.PHON: maka[r|ɾ]i kan sa[r|ɾ]onei
S.TRANSL: the man said:

S.FORM: makasuen ia ipuc-ou na puruto tia avunu misa kan.
S.PHON: makasuen ia ipuʦou na pu[r|ɾ]uto tia avunu misa kan
S.FORM: makasuen ia ipucou na puruto tia avunu misa kan.
S.PHON: makasuen ia ipuʦou na pu[r|ɾ]uto tia avunu misa kan
S.TRANSL: "Well, wrap it in a blanket, we will burry her" he said.

S.FORM: ipucua kan inia manu na puruto pusu'anʉ ka'aan sikam.
S.PHON: ipuʦua kan inia manu na pu[r|ɾ]uto pusuʔanɨ kaʔaan sikam
S.FORM: ipucua kan inia manu na puruto pusu'anʉ ka'aan sikam.
S.PHON: ipuʦua kan inia manu na pu[r|ɾ]uto pusuʔanɨ kaʔaan sikam
S.TRANSL: He wrapped the kid in a blanket, and she moved the kid without a mat.

S.FORM: sua nanakʉ ia ka'aan tavara'ʉ.
S.PHON: sua nanakɨ ia kaʔaan tava[r|ɾ]aʔɨ
S.FORM: sua nanakʉ ia ka'aan tavara'ʉ.
S.PHON: sua nanakɨ ia kaʔaan tava[r|ɾ]aʔɨ
S.TRANSL: As for the woman, she did not realize it.

S.FORM: ni-matapari'i sua manu cacaan.
S.PHON: nimatapa[r|ɾ]iʔi sua manu ʦaʦaan
S.FORM: nimatapari'i sua manu cacaan.
S.PHON: nimatapa[r|ɾ]iʔi sua manu ʦaʦaan
S.TRANSL: She let the child fall on the street.

S.FORM: avici-in sua sikam um-avunʉ sua sikamu esi na cacaan manu ni-matapari'i.
S.PHON: aviʦiin sua sikam umavunɨ sua sikamu esi na ʦaʦaan manu nimatapa[r|ɾ]iʔi
S.FORM: aviciin sua sikam umavunʉ sua sikamu esi na cacaan manu nimatapari'i.
S.PHON: aviʦiin sua sikam umavunɨ sua sikamu esi na ʦaʦaan manu nimatapa[r|ɾ]iʔi
S.TRANSL: She took the mat to burry that mat, it was on the street where she let the child fall.

S.FORM: k<um>oru kan makai na u'aaka k<um>u'oru maamia um-avʉn sua sikam.
S.PHON: kumo[r|ɾ]u kan makai na uʔaaka kumuʔo[r|ɾ]u maamia umavɨn sua sikam
S.FORM: kumoru kan makai na u'aaka kumu'oru maamia umavʉn sua sikam.
S.PHON: kumo[r|ɾ]u kan makai na uʔaaka kumuʔo[r|ɾ]u maamia umavɨn sua sikam
S.TRANSL: She digged a tomb and buried the mat.

S.FORM: sua cʉpʉng-in ia esi teskare-in manu misei.
S.PHON: sua ʦɨpɨŋin ia esi teska[r|ɾ]ein manu misei
S.FORM: sua cʉpʉngin ia esi teskarein manu misei.
S.PHON: sua ʦɨpɨŋin ia esi teska[r|ɾ]ein manu misei
S.TRANSL: She thought she put the kid inside...

S.FORM: akia manu.
S.PHON: akia manu
S.FORM: akia manu.
S.PHON: akia manu
S.TRANSL: But the child wasn't there.

S.FORM: sua manu ia ni-matapari'i cacaan u avunei inia sikam.
S.PHON: sua manu ia nimatapa[r|ɾ]iʔi ʦaʦaan u avunei inia sikam
S.FORM: sua manu ia nimatapari'i cacaan u avunei inia sikam.
S.PHON: sua manu ia nimatapa[r|ɾ]iʔi ʦaʦaan u avunei inia sikam

S.FORM: po'i kan tanasa makasi kan cau.
S.PHON: poʔi kan tanasa makasi kan ʦau
S.FORM: po'i kan tanasa makasi kan cau.
S.PHON: poʔi kan tanasa makasi kan ʦau
S.TRANSL: She returned home and people told her.
She returned home and somebody asked her.

S.FORM: neen tamna manu?
S.PHON: neen tamna manu
S.FORM: neen tamna manu?
S.PHON: neen tamna manu
S.TRANSL: Whom is the kid?

S.FORM: esi cacaan ni-tʉa maku misei kan.
S.PHON: esi ʦaʦaan nitɨa maku misei kan
S.FORM: esi cacaan nitʉa maku misei kan.
S.PHON: esi ʦaʦaan nitɨa maku misei kan
